data.description: This is the positive input supply for the IC switching regulator. A suitable input bypass capacitor must be present at this pin to minimize voltage transients and to supply the switching currents required by the regulator.
data.name: VIN

data.description: Internal switch. The voltage at this pin switches between approximately (+VIN − VSAT) and approximately −0.5 V, with a duty cycle of VOUT / VIN. To minimize coupling to sensitive circuitry, the PCB copper area connected to this pin must be kept to a minimum.
data.name: Output
data.notes: PCB copper area connected to this pin must be kept to a minimum to reduce coupling to sensitive circuitry.

data.description: Senses the regulated output voltage to complete the feedback loop.
data.name: Feedback

data.description: Allows the switching regulator circuit to be shut down using logic signals thus dropping the total input supply current to approximately 80 µA. Pulling this pin below a threshold voltage of approximately 1.3 V turns the regulator on, and pulling this pin above 1.3 V (up to a maximum of 25 V) shuts the regulator down. If this shutdown feature is not required, the ON/OFF pin can be wired to the ground pin or it can be left open. In either case, the regulator will be in the ON condition.
data.name: ON/OFF
data.notes: Active-low shutdown. Pull below ~1.3 V to enable, above ~1.3 V (max 25 V) to shut down. Tie to GND or leave floating to keep regulator ON.
